# MAPLE COURT

## Project wording
- Project name: MAPLE COURT
- Subtitle: Community park for shade and intergenerational activity
- Project phrase: Room for every day
- Location: Toronto
- Everyday uses: walking, accompanying children, quiet sitting, light activity

## Site geometry and records
| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Site area | Approximately 4,882 m² |
| Boundary AB | Approximately 64.1 m |
| Boundary BC | Approximately 76.3 m |
| Boundary CD | Approximately 64.2 m |
| Boundary DA | Approximately 75.9 m |
| Boundary geometry, orientation and surroundings | site-plan.png |
| Site identity and historical surroundings | site-overhead.png |
| Aerial date and source, vertical datum, sampled levels and client flood scenario | source-status.md |
| Existing tree and retained-feature positions | Attached site records |
| Proposed walking loop width | 1.5 m |
| Proposed loop crossfall | 1% |
| Proposed fall across loop width | 15 mm |
| N2–N3 planted separation | Minimum 8 m |

## Zone program
| Zone | Area | Simultaneous users | Principal surface | Shade method | Node |
|---|---:|---:|---|---|---|
| Grove Walk | 1,482 m² | 30 | Compacted crushed stone | Dense tree grove | N1 caregiver seating |
| Play Commons | 1,200 m² | 40 | Broom-finished concrete and 120 m² permeable concrete | Tree canopies and shelters | N2 shared activity |
| Quiet Garden | 1,000 m² | 20 | Compacted crushed stone | Tree canopies | N3 quiet seating |
| Open Lawn | 1,200 m² | 35 | Grass with a compacted crushed-stone path | Tree canopies at the edge | N4 gentle exercise |
| Total | 4,882 m² | 125 | Paths included within zone areas | Summer layout | N1–N4 |

## Shade areas
| Cover | Walking and sitting surface area |
|---|---:|
| Tree canopy footprint | 720 m² |
| Shelter footprint | 180 m² |
| Combined separate footprints | 900 m² |

## New planting palette
| Code | Botanical name | Layer | Planting size | Quantity |
|---|---|---|---|---:|
| AR | Acer rubrum | Tree | 60 mm trunk caliper | 6 |
| QR | Quercus rubra | Tree | 60 mm trunk caliper | 6 |
| CO | Celtis occidentalis | Tree | 60 mm trunk caliper | 6 |
| CS | Cornus sericea | Shrub | 600 mm height | 36 |
| CP | Carex pensylvanica | Groundcover | 90 mm pot diameter | 240 |

## Materials
| Element | Material and construction |
|---|---|
| Walking loop | Compacted crushed stone; 1.5 m clear width; 1% crossfall |
| N2 permeable area | 120 m²; 120 mm permeable concrete over 200 mm open-graded aggregate |
| Other Play Commons paving | Broom-finished concrete |
| Seating | Timber slats on galvanized steel frames |
| Planting edges | Steel edging |
| Shelter | Timber slat canopy on galvanized steel posts |

## Node relationships and scene states
- N1: caregiver seating with a view toward N2
- N2: shared activity within Play Commons
- N3: quiet seating within Quiet Garden
- N4: gentle exercise at the Open Lawn edge
- Summer daytime state: 12:00
- Summer nighttime state: 21:00
- N2 scene pair: one shared camera position
- N3 scene pair: one shared camera position
- N4 scene pair: one shared camera position

## Implementation areas
| Phase | Zones | Area | Scope |
|---|---|---:|---|
| Phase 1 | Grove Walk; Quiet Garden | 2,482 m² | N1 and N3, associated paths, planting, seating and lighting |
| Phase 2 | Play Commons; Open Lawn | 2,400 m² | N2 and N4, associated paths, planting, shelters, permeable concrete and lighting |

# MAPLE COURT — real site, historical baseline

The supplied inputs are site-overhead.png (a real 2022 orthorectified aerial with a marked design extent) and site-plan.png (a deterministic context plan derived from the recorded source geometry), plus this text. The two boards share the same projection, boundary A–D, north direction and scale. Neither contains a proposed park layout. The tested system receives the two PNG boards and this text.

## Actual site and design extent

The site is the former surface car park at 34 Hanna Avenue, Toronto. The municipal parcel record 5493560 has an effective date in 2017 and an area of 4,881.8053 m². This benchmark uses that irregular parcel as an approximately 4,882 m² community park design extent; it is not an 80 × 50 m rectangle. Its sides A–B, B–C, C–D and D–A are approximately 64.1, 76.3, 64.2 and 75.9 m. North is grid north in NAD83(CSRS) / MTM zone 10 (EPSG:2952). Published coordinate precision does not establish a new survey accuracy.

Liberty Street is north of the site, Hanna Avenue east and Atlantic Avenue west. Existing buildings and parking south of the boundary remain outside the design extent. The aerial shows the historical parking use, adjoining buildings, streets and vegetation. Existing asphalt inside the extent may be replaced by the proposed park. Propose connections to the adjoining street sidewalks; the precise curb geometry and opening dimensions have not been surveyed.

The plan includes selected neighbouring footprints from the City's 2022 3D massing archive, compared with the 2022 aerial. Blank plan areas do not imply vacant land: use the aerial for complete visible context. Road centrelines were extracted from the current municipal service in 2026 and compared with the historical image; they are not a 2022 road survey. Gray road bands are indicative corridors, not measured road widths. The parcel, building archive and imagery have different dates and must not be described as a single survey campaign.

No verified tree inventory, species, tree centres, protection radii or spot elevations are supplied. MAPLE COURT is the project name, not evidence of three existing maple trees. Retain visible established vegetation where feasible and clearly distinguish proposed planting from existing vegetation; do not invent surveyed tree identities. Additional planting is allowed. Any proposed grading is a design assumption, not a measured existing level.

This is a historical design exercise based on 2022 imagery. The City's later interim park and future park proposals are outside the input baseline and must not be copied as an answer. The chosen extent does not assert land ownership, planning approval or construction readiness.

## Sources, dates and reuse

- Aerial: City of Toronto 2022 orthophotography, native 8 cm ground sampling, exported at 25 cm per pixel for this context crop. Native pixel spacing is not positional accuracy. [Official map service](https://gis.toronto.ca/arcgis/rest/services/basemap/cot_ortho_2022_color_8cm/MapServer).
- Boundary: [City property boundaries](https://open.toronto.ca/dataset/property-boundaries/), parcel 5493560, municipal record effective in 2017; retrieved 2026-09-06.
- Selected building outlines: [City 3D massing](https://open.toronto.ca/dataset/3d-massing/), 2022 archive; retrieved 2026-09-06. Current road centrelines are dated by their 2026-09-06 extraction, not relabelled 2022.
- Historical use and later change: [City project page](https://www.toronto.ca/city-government/planning-development/construction-new-facilities/park-facility-projects/new-park-at-34-hanna-avenue/). Used only to establish chronology; no proposal drawing is included.

The official dataset pages specify the [Open Government Licence – Toronto](https://open.toronto.ca/open-data-licence/), which permits attributed reuse and adaptation subject to its terms. Two raw catalogue licence fields are unspecified; the official dataset pages and licence text are the cited rights evidence. No City endorsement is claimed. All source downloads were made on 2026-09-06. Author-side raw geometry, source requests and checks are retained for reproduction and are not additional benchmark inputs.

steps.userMessage:
MAPLE COURT | Community park for shade and intergenerational activity

We are turning the Toronto site shown in the attached aerial into a neighborhood park for walking, accompanying children, quiet sitting and light activity. The project name is "MAPLE COURT". Work within the existing A–D boundary: approximately 4,882 m², with AB 64.1 m, BC 76.3 m, CD 64.2 m and DA 75.9 m. Preserve the positions of existing trees and retained features recorded in the attached site information. The aerial supplies the site's recognizable surroundings.

Organize four zones: Grove Walk, 1,482 m²; Play Commons, 1,200 m²; Quiet Garden, 1,000 m²; and Open Lawn, 1,200 m². Paths count within these areas. Provide a continuous 1.5 m walking loop with a proposed 1% crossfall, a dense planted grove and an open grass area. The summer layout needs 900 m² of covered walking and sitting surfaces: 720 m² beneath tree canopies and 180 m² beneath shelters, counted as separate footprints. Add 18 trees and the shrub and groundcover layers listed in the fact sheet. Place 120 m² of permeable concrete within Play Commons. Four nodes organize daily use: N1 caregiver seating in Grove Walk, N2 shared activity in Play Commons, N3 quiet seating in Quiet Garden and N4 gentle exercise in Open Lawn. Separate N2 and N3 with a planted strip at least 8 m wide. Print the project name and "Room for every day" on the masterplan and planting schedule; repeat the zone names and botanical names exactly between those two deliverables.

Audience: neighborhood residents and the parks team, deciding the preferred layout and the scope of the next design stage.

Inputs (attached): 01-client-facts.en.md records the site dimensions, area schedule, planting quantities and activity requirements. 02-delivery-catalog.en.md lists the deliverables, proportions, formats and stages. site-overhead.png is the identity source, showing the real historical aerial and surrounding context. site-plan.png is the constraint source for the existing boundary, north, scale and surroundings. source-status.md records the aerial's date, source and reuse terms, the measured design extent and the site assumptions.

Deliverables:
1. Three distinct landscape direction boards, one each for a grove-led layout, a shelter-led layout and a sequence of connected activity clearings
2. One selection record naming the chosen direction and three reasons tied to shade, through-walking and the relationship between N2 and N3
3. One two-page site analysis and zone schedule for the selected direction, with zone names, areas, capacities, paving, shade methods and the five botanical names
4. One developed masterplan with activity zoning, north arrow, scale bar, boundary dimensions, retained features, the walking loop and lighting positions
5. One shade and planting sheet with canopy and shelter footprints, three planting layers, and a plant and material schedule
6. One dimensioned section through the walking loop and N2, with the crossfall and permeable concrete construction
7. Two node sheets, one for N1 caregiver seating and one for N2 shared activity, each with a plan, dimensions and a perspective
8. Two matching N2 perspectives from one camera position, at 12:00 and 21:00 in summer
9. One 10-second park sequence following the loop from N1 to N2, with daytime activity and an evening view of N2
10. One presentation document of at least eight pages, reusing the directions, selection, zone schedule, masterplan, planting, section and scenes

Acceptance:
- The three direction boards explore the three named approaches within the A–D boundary; the selection record chooses one before the site analysis, and the masterplan and presentation opening page identify that same direction.
- The site analysis, masterplan, shade and planting sheet and presentation repeat Grove Walk 1,482 m², Play Commons 1,200 m², Quiet Garden 1,000 m² and Open Lawn 1,200 m², together with the five botanical names and plant codes in the fact sheet. The masterplan, planting schedule and presentation print MAPLE COURT and Room for every day.
- The masterplan labels the four boundary lengths, preserves recorded trees and retained features, identifies N1–N4 and lighting positions, and dimensions at least 8 m of planting between N2 and N3; its zone capacities match the site analysis: 30, 40, 20 and 35 people respectively.
- The shade and planting sheet and masterplan agree on the dense grove, open grass area, 720 m² of canopy-covered surfaces, 180 m² of shelter-covered surfaces and 120 m² of permeable concrete. The planting schedule totals 18 new trees, 36 shrubs and 240 groundcover plants.
- The section and N2 node sheet agree on the 1.5 m loop, 1% crossfall, 15 mm fall, and 120 mm permeable concrete over 200 mm open-graded aggregate; the N1 sheet shows caregiver seating facing N2.
- The N2 perspectives show the same camera and furnishings at 12:00 and 21:00; the 10-second video follows the masterplan's N1–N2 route and repeats those node designs. The presentation contains at least eight pages and reuses the selected scheme's drawings, zone areas, planting names and both time states.

Please clearly mark which version you consider the final deliverable. If nothing is marked, the last exported version counts.
